components.note: A friend at the base — the object of the affection.
A roof: welcoming the friend into one's home.
A reaching hand at the top.

story: A hand reaching out to bring a friend (友) in under one's roof (冖) — welcoming someone you care for into your home. The classical form also held 心 (heart) in the middle; the simplified form keeps the gesture, not the heart.
Two strokes bending apart — the original sense was "to divide." It was borrowed early on for the number eight, and the dividing sense lives on in 分 (fēn, to split), which contains it.

components.note: The meaning half — 父 is the formal word for father.
Lends the sound bā.

story: The formal "father" 父 on top for meaning, with 巴 (bā) underneath supplying the sound — giving the everyday, affectionate bà.

components.note: The mouth radical — this is a spoken particle, so the meaning lives in the mouth.
Lends the sound ba.

story: A mouth (口) marking it as speech, plus 巴 for sound. As a sentence-final particle it softens a command or suggestion into "...okay?"; as a noun (bā) it transliterates the English "bar."

A pictograph of a flame or the rising sun casting light — light being the essence of whiteness and brightness. Beyond "white" it stretches to "clear/plain" (明白 to understand) and "in vain" (白 for nothing).

components.note: A single stroke on top — a number sign, hinting this is a counting word.
Lends the sound (bái → bǎi).

story: The number-marker 一 (one) sitting over 白 (bái) for sound — a hundred, the round number that caps the basic counting run.

components.note: Two pieces of jade (王 is jade in this position), one on each side.
A knife in the middle, dividing the jade.

story: A knife (刂) splitting a piece of jade (玉) into two halves — from "to divide" came the sense of a divided group: a class, team, or work shift.

components.note: The dividing strokes (丷) up top — splitting in two.
An ox below: an ox was a big thing to divide up evenly.

story: The splitting mark (八/丷) over an ox (牛) — dividing something large right down the middle. Hence "half."

compounds.en: half a day; a long while

components.note: Supplies the sound bāng — and, loosely, the sense of a body of people.
A cloth or banner below.

story: A nation (邦) over a cloth (巾) — a banner a group rallies under. From standing together came the meaning "to help." 邦 also carries the sound.

compounds.en: to help out, do a favor

components.note: The wrapping radical — an arm curling around something. Also carries the sound.
A curled-up baby inside, being wrapped.

story: An arm (勹) curling around a baby (巳) — to swaddle, to wrap up. From there: a bundle, a bag, and "to include."

components.note: The wood radical — cups were once carved from wood.
Lends the sound (bù → bēi).

story: The wood radical (木) marks the material of an old cup, with 不 supplying the sound — a cup or glass.

components.note: Two people drawn back-to-back — the left one mirrored.

story: Two people sitting back-to-back. Houses traditionally faced south, so your back was to the north — and the character was borrowed for "north." The original "back" sense was rewritten as 背 (bèi), which still contains it.

components.note: A foot/going element on top — heading out.
A field below — the destination.

story: Going out (夂) to the field (田) to get ready for the harvest — to prepare, to have on hand.

components.note: A whole tree.
A stroke across the base, pointing at the roots.

story: A tree (木) with a mark drawn across its base to point at the roots — the "root, origin, source." By extension: the root/original thing, and the measure word for books (the root text).

components.note: Two people side by side, facing the same way. Also carries the sound.

story: Two figures standing right next to each other, facing the same direction — placing two things side by side: to compare.

components.note: The movement radical — a border is where you walk to the edge of.
The simplified form's inner part; the full form 邊 had a more complex phonetic 臱.

story: The walking radical (辶) framing the character — the edge you reach by going outward: a side, a border, an edge.

components.note: "Another / separate" on the left.
The knife radical — cutting apart.

story: A knife (刂) cutting things into separate parts (另) — "to separate, distinguish, part." From "set apart" come both "other/another" and the negative command "don't" (別 = don't do that).

components.note: The sickness radical — a person on a bed. Almost every illness word carries it.
Lends the sound (bǐng → bìng).

story: The sickness radical (疒), a person laid up on a bed, wrapping 丙 for sound — illness, disease, to fall ill.
